description: Backend ML data layer: the GPS validator (pure logic), the traffic prediction engine (reads segment_speed_observations, falls back to baseline), the segment-ingestion helper that closes the gps_observations->segment_speed_observations gap, and migration 016 with the 5 tables + indexes + 12 seeded Dar es Salaam road_segments. These are the foundation FEAT-002 wires in; they compile standalone and leave the codebase building (new files, not yet referenced).
steps: Create services/api-gateway/src/services/GpsValidator.ts (create the src/services/ directory). Define `interface GpsObservation { lat:number; lng:number; speed_kmh:number; heading:number; accuracy_m?:number; timestamp:number }` and `interface ValidationResult { valid:boolean; rejection_reason?: 'impossible_speed'|'low_accuracy'|'stale'|'duplicate'|'impossible_jump'|'out_of_bounds' }`. Export `function haversineMeters(lat1,lng1,lat2,lng2):number` (R=6371000, proper haversine) and `function validateGpsObservation(obs: GpsObservation, previous?: GpsObservation): ValidationResult`. Rules in order, return first failure: speed_kmh>150 -> impossible_speed; accuracy_m!=null && accuracy_m>50 -> low_accuracy; outside Tanzania (lat<-11.7 || lat>-0.99 || lng<29.3 || lng>40.5) -> out_of_bounds; Date.now()-obs.timestamp>30000 -> stale; vs previous: haversineMeters>500 in <5000ms -> impossible_jump; haversineMeters<1 within 2000ms -> duplicate. Keep a module-level `Map<string, GpsObservation>` of last observation per driver so duplicate/impossible_jump work across calls when no explicit previous is passed; an explicit `previous` arg overrides. No DB import.

Create services/api-gateway/src/services/TrafficPredictor.ts. `import { Pool } from 'pg'; import { pool } from '../database/connection';` is NOT needed at module top-level for the functions to compile — accept `pool: Pool` as a parameter (the routes pass it). Export: `predictTraffic(segmentIds:string[], departureTime:string|number|Date, pool:Pool):Promise<PredictionResult[]>` returning `{segment_id, road_name, predicted_speed_kmh, status:'jam'|'slow'|'clear', color, confidence, model_type:'ml'|'baseline'|'insufficient_data', observations_used}`. For each segment compute Dar-local day_of_week (Sun=0..Sat=6) and hour_of_day (UTC+3 with day rollover). Query segment_speed_observations for (segment_id, day_of_week, hour_of_day); >=10 rows -> ml (speed=AVG(observed_speed_kmh), confidence=clamp(0.7..0.95) from count & stddev); 1..9 rows -> insufficient_data (baseline speed, conf 0.30); 0 rows -> baseline (baseline speed, conf 0.35); segment_id not in road_segments -> insufficient_data (generic clear 50 km/h, conf 0.10, road_name=segment_id). Status/color thresholds: <15 jam red #ff3b30; 15-35 slow orange #ff9500; >35 clear green #00d46a. Baseline rules: Mon-Fri (day 1-5) hours 6-8 and 16-18 -> jam(8) on major roads {nyerere-s-001,morogoro-001,kilwa-001,pugu-001}, slow(25) otherwise in those windows; all other times + Sat/Sun -> clear(50).

In the same TrafficPredictor.ts export `findBestDepartureTime(segmentIds:string[], fromTime:string|number|Date, pool:Pool):Promise<{from_time,best_time,savings_minutes,total_minutes_at_from,total_minutes_at_best}>`: test 12 slots (fromTime, +15m ... +180m); per slot sum segment travel minutes = length_m/(predicted_speed_kmh*1000/60) using predictTraffic; best_time = min total; savings_minutes = total_at_from - total_at_best. Resolve road_segments length_m via the predictTraffic road lookup (cache the road_segments query per call).

In the same TrafficPredictor.ts export `async function ingestObservationToSegment(obs:{driver_id:string; trip_id?:string|null; lat:number; lng:number; speed_kmh:number; observed_at:Date}, pool:Pool):Promise<void>` and helper `nearestSegment(lat,lng, segments):{id:string; distance_m:number}|null` (perpendicular distance via equirectangular projection; tolerance 75 m). SELECT all road_segments, find nearest within tolerance; if found, compute Dar day_of_week/hour_of_day from observed_at and INSERT into segment_speed_observations(segment_id, day_of_week, hour_of_day, observed_speed_kmh, trip_id, observed_at). Skip silently if no segment within tolerance or speed_kmh is null.

Create services/api-gateway/migrations/016_gps_ml_pipeline.sql. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for: gps_observations(id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), driver_id UUID NOT NULL, trip_id UUID, lat DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, lng DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, speed_kmh DOUBLE PRECISION, heading DOUBLE PRECISION, accuracy_m DOUBLE PRECISION, obs_timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, is_valid BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false, rejection_reason TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()); road_segments(id TEXT PK, road_name TEXT NOT NULL, lat_start DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, lng_start DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, lat_end DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, lng_end DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, length_m INTEGER, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()); segment_speed_observations(id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), segment_id TEXT NOT NULL, day_of_week INTEGER NOT NULL, hour_of_day INTEGER NOT NULL, observed_speed_kmh DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, trip_id UUID, observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()); ml_model_versions(id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), model_type TEXT, version TEXT, training_samples INTEGER, accuracy_mae DOUBLE PRECISION, trained_at TIMESTAMPTZ, is_active BOOLEAN, notes TEXT); traffic_predictions_cache(id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), segment_id TEXT, predicted_for TIMESTAMPTZ, predicted_speed_kmh DOUBLE PRECISION, confidence DOUBLE PRECISION, model_version_id UUID, model_type TEXT, expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()). CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS: idx_gps_obs_driver ON gps_observations(driver_id); idx_gps_obs_trip ON gps_observations(trip_id); idx_gps_obs_timestamp ON gps_observations(obs_timestamp); idx_gps_obs_valid ON gps_observations(is_valid); idx_seg_speed_segment ON segment_speed_observations(segment_id); idx_seg_speed_window ON segment_speed_observations(day_of_week,hour_of_day); idx_traffic_cache_segment ON traffic_predictions_cache(segment_id,predicted_for). acceptance_criteria: services/api-gateway/src/services/GpsValidator.ts exists and exports validateGpsObservation + haversineMeters with the exact interface and rule set.

services/api-gateway/src/services/TrafficPredictor.ts exists and exports predictTraffic, findBestDepartureTime, ingestObservationToSegment with the documented model_type/confidence/baseline semantics.
services/api-gateway/migrations/016_gps_ml_pipeline.sql exists with all 5 tables, the 7 named indexes, and the 12 seeded road_segments (ids and coordinates verbatim).
`cd services/api-gateway && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E 'GpsValidator|TrafficPredictor' | grep -v node_modules` outputs nothing (0 TypeScript errors).
verification: cd services/api-gateway && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -E 'GpsValidator|TrafficPredictor' | grep -v node_modules  -> expect empty output
findings: All three files created and compile with 0 TS errors. pool.query<T> generic required a locally-declared interface (not an inline type alias) to satisfy the pg typings under strict:false. ObsMap typed as Map<string, ObsRow>. GpsObservation.timestamp is mandatory in the interface but callers should default it to Date.now() before calling validateGpsObservation (per CRITICAL RULES). nearestSegment exported for use by FEAT-002's tracking.ts wiring.
